label: PRE-REGISTERED v1.2 EXPECTATIONS (D125), committed BEFORE any v1.2 commit was run against them. The Part 2 expectations in scenario_preregistration.json stay EXACTLY as they were; nothing there is revised. A wrong expectation is recorded as an erratum with its reason, as E1 was.
v12_design_summary: two timescales: dispatch unchanged at H = 0.5 s, and a per-RC-job PLAN chosen once at admission by fleet-wide DeltaJ against DECLINE over the job lifetime, with reserved release times and logged re-plans

P1.scenario: plan chosen at admission: one robot question, idle GPU, cold 11k history
P1.expect_detail: a job plan is chosen ONCE at admission, is logged, and is a member of the feasible plan set; it is not DECLINE, since S1 already shows this question is servable on an idle engine
P1.justification: v1.2 chooses a plan once at admission by fleet-wide DeltaJ against DECLINE; S1 passing on v1.0 and v1.1 establishes the question is servable, so DECLINE here would be a regression

P2.scenario: reservation semantics: an admitted plan on an otherwise quiet fleet
P2.expect_detail: each reserved unit is released at its planned time within one decision period (0.1 s), OR earlier only where the short-horizon rollout scored the earlier release strictly better, which must be visible
P2.justification: D125 reservation rule: planned units are released AT their planned times, with earlier release on an idle GPU only if the short horizon scores it strictly better

P3.scenario: no silent deferral: every admitted plan over a 600 s seed-0 fleet run
P3.expect_detail: ZERO planned units that are neither released nor accounted for by a logged re-plan. A unit that simply never happens, with no re-plan logged, is a failure
P3.justification: D125 states re-plan, never silent deferral, and requires every re-plan to be logged with its cause; silent deferral is the v1.0 failure mode this design exists to remove

P4.expect_detail: when a unit completes later than planned and predicted completion with kappa then exceeds D_r, a re-plan is logged with cause (a)

P5.scenario: re-plan on a believed readiness tier change (cause c)
P5.expect_detail: a re-plan is logged with cause (c) when the believed tier of the question history changes
P5.realisability: my S6 showed I cannot drive a HOST-WARM belief from the trace interface, so a tier change may be undrivable; if no tier change occurs this is reported NOT REALISABLE and is not scored

P6.scenario: ABANDON is reachable: a question whose remainder cannot meet D_r after a late unit
P6.expect_detail: ABANDON is chosen at the re-plan, the remainder is declined, and the state value of what is built is kept. BOTH halves are checked: that ABANDON is chosen, and that the retained state value is non-zero
P6.justification: D125 makes ABANDON one option at re-plan and defines it as keeping the state value of what is built; if that value is structurally zero the option is inert, which F-A2 makes a live risk

P7.scenario: plan_latest signature: a question with ample slack, switch ON against OFF
P7.expect_detail: with plan_latest ON the first planned release is strictly later than with it OFF, for a question with slack; with it OFF the first piece starts now
P7.justification: PIECES(b)-LATEST places the first piece at t_ls(b), the latest safe start, so the switch must have an observable signature or it is a dead switch

P8.scenario: kappa monotonicity: the same question at kappa = 1 and kappa > 1
P8.expect_detail: the latest safe start with kappa > 1 is at or earlier than with kappa = 1, so a larger safety factor never starts later
P8.justification: kappa inflates predicted completion, so it can only tighten the latest safe start; the opposite would mean the safety factor is applied with the wrong sign

P9.scenario: state value at T_r: is the channel still structurally zero under v1.2
P9.expect_detail: the state-value channel is NOT exactly zero for every planned RC candidate. If it is exactly zero everywhere, then v1.2 Jhat term "state value at T_r" and ABANDON keeping "the state value of what is built" are BOTH inert, which is a gate-relevant failure and must be reported as one
P9.justification: F-A2 measured state value exactly zero for all 124,354 candidates under v1.0 and v1.1; v1.2 depends on that term twice, so it has to be tested explicitly rather than assumed fixed

P10.scenario: two-timescale separation: zero-tie rate for planned RC units
P10.expect_detail: the fraction of planned RC release candidates whose DeltaJ is exactly zero is far below v1.1 measured 0.723 for rc_piece releases, because planned units are released at their planned times rather than re-scored every period
P10.justification: D125 states v1.1 per-piece release scoring, the source of the 72 percent zero ties, does NOT apply to planned RC units, so the tie rate is the direct observable of that claim

ablations_to_score.v1.2: planner_rc + plan_latest + replan ON, plus B1, F2, F3 ON, F1 and F4 OFF
ablations_to_score.planner_off: v1.1 behaviour: planner_rc OFF, B1 + F2 + F3 ON

gate_definition.half_1: every pre-registered behaviour scenario passes for v1.2
gate_definition.half_2: the offline comparison is at least as good as the BEST baseline among edf, llf and always-cloud-fcfs at EVERY size in 4, 8, 16, 32 on BOTH the dashcam and the robot measure
gate_definition.label: the comparison remains SCREENING and OPTIMISTIC FOR COVEX, since the dry run prices the engine from the same committed curves COVEX model uses

carried_forward.F_A2: state value exactly zero over 124,354 candidates; v1.2 depends on it twice, tested by P9
carried_forward.F_A7: COVEX was also worse on dashcams, 48.7 and 7.5 percent of instants at 8 and 16 devices against edf 99.9 and 62.6, so the gate is judged on BOTH axes at EVERY size

decisions_provisional: plan observability: if v1.2 does not log the chosen plan and its planned release times in the decision log or arm stats, the planner entry point is wrapped from inside policy/audit/ to record them; no v1.2 file is edited
P2 tolerance: one decision period, 0.1 s
P7 and P8 are comparative scenarios, run twice with the switch or kappa changed and compared, since neither has an absolute expected value
best baseline for half 2 is the maximum over edf, llf and always-cloud-fcfs per size and per axis, computed from the same run
ablations that need a plan type forced are run through the documented switches; if v1.2 exposes no such switch they are reported NOT RUNNABLE rather than approximated

_provenance.n: crafted event lists, development data only, seed 0
